findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the harness handles a filter emission that violates the contract (FAIL emitted anyway, out-of-vocabulary value, or unparseable output): parse-validate the response and define the fallback (recommend coercing any non-PASS to ABSTAIN so the residual risk stays 'false-PASS or under-coverage', never false-reject).
evidence: Plan step 3: 'emit per AC either PASS(with citations) or ABSTAIN. The contract forbids FAIL.'

ABSENCE: a forbidden token is a soft prompt-level prohibition, not a mechanical guarantee; the plan specifies no parse/validation fallback (e.g. treat an illegal emission as ABSTAIN, or fail the run) so the residual-risk measurement of false-PASSes could silently mis-bucket a violating emission.
findings.finding: The filter LLM contract (PASS/ABSTAIN, FAIL forbidden) has no specified handler for a contract-violating or malformed emission — if the single no-tools LLM call returns FAIL anyway, or an unparseable/out-of-vocabulary value, the harness behavior is undefined.
findings.location: Protocol step 3 (Filter pass) / AC 'filter+fallback ... run end-to-end'
scenarios: The LLM emits FAIL for an AC despite the prohibition — is it dropped, coerced to ABSTAIN, or counted as a filter reject (which the design claims is impossible by construction)?
The LLM emits a value not in {PASS, ABSTAIN} or malformed JSON/citations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3: validate the per-AC emission against the {PASS, ABSTAIN} vocabulary; treat any illegal or unparseable emission (including a forbidden FAIL) as ABSTAIN so it flows to the agentic fallback, and log the violation count as a reported failure mode.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete default per-AC pack-size cap (e.g. a char/token budget) in step 2, so the coverage and false-PASS numbers are reproducible.
evidence: 'Cap per-AC pack size; record pack-build failures honestly'
Pack size is load-bearing for the coverage and false-PASS metrics that are the experiment deliverable
findings.finding: Step 2 says 'Cap per-AC pack size' but never states the cap value, leaving a tunable the executor must choose without guidance; since pack size directly affects filter coverage and false-PASS risk (the two things being measured), an unstated cap makes results non-reproducible.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a stated default, e.g. 'cap each per-AC pack at ~2000 chars of evidence slices; if evidence exceeds the cap, truncate and note the truncation in the pack-build log.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item 'Harness exists in the experiment worktree (throwaway; NOT pushed to Gerrit; no s' cites operational evidence (merge_gate) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Specify the fallback path when zero ACs abstain: skip the agentic run and report cost = filter-only (agentic = 0), rather than reducing to an empty AC block that raises CompletionRecoveryError.
evidence: completion_criteria.py:84-85: `if not criteria: raise CompletionRecoveryError(...)`
completion.py:227-229 catches it → criteria_count = 0 (pre-flight only), but verdict production still enumerates
Plan step 3 contract: filter emits PASS or ABSTAIN; 100% coverage → empty abstained set
Plan step 4b: cost delta = (filter call + narrowed agentic run) vs full agentic run
findings.finding: The plan does not specify fallback behavior when the filter PASSes ALL criteria (zero ABSTAINed ACs) — the experiment's ideal success case. Reducing the AC block to empty makes explicit_completion_criteria raise CompletionRecoveryError for a non-bug ticket, so the 'narrowed agentic run' has no criteria to verify and the cost-delta metric is undefined for that ticket.
findings.location: Protocol step 4 / step 4b (cost delta) & AC line 'coverage ... cost deltas'; vs src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_criteria.py:84-85
scenarios: A ground-truth-met ticket where the filter achieves 100% coverage — precisely the outcome the experiment is trying to demonstrate
findings.suggested_fix: When the abstained set is empty, record the narrowed-arm cost as the filter LLM call alone (no agentic run) and note the full-agentic control still runs for the delta.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief prior-art note situating the FILTER+fallback design as an LLM-cascade-with-abstention / selective-prediction pattern (cite e.g. arXiv 2502.09054 'Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention'), and use it to frame the coverage-vs-false-PASS metrics and go/no-go verdict against known expectations and cascade reliability ceilings.
evidence: Plan: 'use the single pass as a FILTER that may only PASS or ABSTAIN per criterion (never reject), then run the existing agentic verifier scoped to the remaining criteria' — this is a two-stage LLM cascade with abstention.
Plan frames the design as an 'Operator counter-proposal to test' with no reference to existing work.

Retrieved: 'Cost-Saving LLM Cascades with Early Abstention' (arXiv.org/html/2502.09054) — 'combines ... selective prediction, which aims at reducing the error rate by allowing models to abstain ... and LLM cascades, which focus on combining small and large LLMs to reduce cost.' Directly matches the filter-abstain-then-escalate design.

Retrieved: 'The Art of Abstention: Selective Prediction and Error Regularization' (aclanthology.org/2021.acl-long.84.pdf) — abstain-on-low-confidence classification, the general form of the FILTER contract.

Retrieved: 'LLM Verifier Cascades: Correlation and Reliability Ceilings' (cctest.ai) — 'correlated LLM verifier cascades may yield polynomial, not exponential, reliability gains and can saturate under blind spots' — directly bears on the plan's residual risk of false-PASS and coverage.

ABSENCE: the plan's residual-risk framing ('false-positive PASSes and insufficient coverage') restates the precision/abstention-rate frontier without naming or drawing on the literature that already models it.
findings.finding: The FILTER + narrowed-agentic-fallback design is a textbook 'LLM cascade with abstention' / selective-prediction pattern, but the plan derives it solely from operator dialogue and considers no prior art — even though the published literature already characterizes the exact coverage-vs-false-PASS tradeoff (and reliability ceilings) the experiment sets out to measure.
findings.location: Plan sections 'Why' and 'Protocol' steps 3-4 (filter PASS/ABSTAIN, escalate abstained criteria to agentic verifier)
scenarios: The experiment reports a coverage/false-PASS result that the cascade-with-abstention literature would have predicted or contextualized (e.g., correlated-verifier ceiling), and the go/no-go verdict lacks a baseline expectation to compare against.
Productization recommendation is made without benchmarking against known threshold-tuning / Pareto-frontier techniques from the routing/cascade literature.
findings.suggested_fix: In 'Why', note that the single-pass-filter-then-escalate structure is an instance of the established LLM-cascade-with-abstention / selective-prediction pattern (the plan's 'coverage' = abstention rate; 'false-PASS' = filter precision). Reference the literature (e.g. arXiv 2502.09054; the correlated-verifier reliability-ceiling result) so the metrics table and verdict can state whether observed results meet, beat, or fall short of published cascade-abstention behavior, and so the go/no-go recommendation accounts for known blind-spot/ceiling failure modes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Frame the filter contract positively via a closed output schema whose only legal values are PASS and ABSTAIN, rather than instructing the model that FAIL is forbidden, to avoid the pink-elephant effect of naming the forbidden token.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'The contract forbids FAIL.'

ABSENCE: the plan gives no positive-framing alternative (e.g. an output schema whose value set is literally {PASS, ABSTAIN}) that would structurally exclude FAIL rather than mentioning it as forbidden.
findings.finding: The filter contract is stated as a negative prohibition ('The contract forbids FAIL'), a pink-elephant/instruction-locality antipattern that names the forbidden token and can induce the very FAIL output it aims to suppress.
scenarios: Prompt author renders the contract to the model as a rule mentioning FAIL, increasing the chance the model reaches for it under uncertainty instead of ABSTAIN.
findings.suggested_fix: State the contract as: 'each AC MUST be exactly one of PASS (with citations) or ABSTAIN' and constrain the emission to that closed vocabulary, omitting any mention of FAIL from the prompt.

findings.checklist_item: Account for the 8,000-char description admission cap: keep adversarial edits length-neutral (or below cap) and state that the harness detects/reports precheck short-circuits distinctly from agentic verdicts.
evidence: gate_ops.py:79 `description_limit = _config.load_config(ctx.repo_root).verify.max_ticket_description_chars`
gate_ops.py:81-104: description_chars > description_limit → deterministic_child_failure with run_verify=False
_config_schema.py:152 `max_ticket_description_chars: int = 8_000`
Plan step 1: corpus 'near the 8000-char cap ... (7998 chars)' plus adversarial 'copies ... with 1-2 ACs edited'
findings.finding: The completion precheck deterministically FAILs any ticket whose description exceeds verify.max_ticket_description_chars (default 8,000) before any agentic verify runs, but the corpus targets descriptions near the 8,000-char cap and the adversarial variants edit AC text — an edit that pushes a 7998-char ticket over 8,000 yields a deterministic precheck FAIL, not the agentic PASS/FAIL the experiment measures.
scenarios: Adversarial variant of the 7998-char tapeworm ticket where the edited/unmet AC adds characters, crossing 8,000
Any control-arm run of an un-reduced near-cap ticket if the store copy is marginally above 8,000
findings.suggested_fix: Constrain adversarial edits to not increase description length past verify.max_ticket_description_chars, and have the harness assert run_verify was reached (not a deterministic precheck FAIL) before recording a verdict.
